chapters.question_prompt: Q1: What Exactly Is Heir Hunting?
chapters.title: What Exactly Is Heir Hunting?
chapters.subtitle: Three adjacent businesses with different claimants, rules and evidence.
chapters.executive_summary: Heir hunting is evidence work that connects a legally entitled person to an asset or estate, not a universal license to collect abandoned money. Three adjacent lanes share public records but differ in authority: intestate probate research, state custodial unclaimed property, and foreclosure or tax-sale surplus recovery. Choose the lane before calculating a fee or contacting a claimant. This chapter turns public records into a documented research queue, distinguishes kinship from entitlement, and replaces brittle portal scraping with permissioned data access, source provenance, and measurable case qualification.

key_metrics.label: Legal lanes
key_metrics.note: Probate, custodial property, and surplus are distinct.

key_metrics.label: Qualified yield
key_metrics.note: A research funnel, not an expected recovery rate.

sections.heading: Separate the three businesses before accepting a file
paragraphs: Intestate probate heir research asks which people inherit property that passes without an effective testamentary disposition. California Probate Code section 6402 supplies an order of succession for the part of an intestate estate not passing to a surviving spouse under section 6401, or the entire intestate estate when there is no surviving spouse. Start with the death certificate, probate petition, docket, and any will or trust references; a surname match does not establish intestacy. A personal representative may commission genealogy, but the probate court resolves disputed rights and supervises distribution through applicable proceedings. Your deliverable is a sourced family reconstruction and evidentiary packet, not a private declaration that someone owns a percentage of the decedent's assets.

State custodial unclaimed property concerns a holder's transfer of dormant property to a state administrator for the owner's benefit. The claimant may be a living individual, corporation, estate, or successor, so this lane often needs identity and authority documents rather than an extended family tree. California's State Controller administers the state claim process; it does not become the probate court merely because an account owner died. Locate the property identifier, reported owner, former address, reporting holder, and available property description. Then establish the claimant's right to that particular item. An heir who proves kinship may still need estate authority or another permitted succession procedure before the Controller can release funds to the appropriate recipient.

Foreclosure and tax-sale surplus recovery concerns proceeds left after legally prioritized payments, not a dormant bank account waiting in a state database. California Civil Code section 2924k orders distribution of trustee-sale proceeds, including sale expenses, secured obligations, junior interests, and the remaining balance to the trustor or successor as specified. Tax-sale excess proceeds follow a different statutory process; do not transplant the trustee-sale sequence into a tax file. Identify whether the custodian is a trustee, court, county tax collector, or clerk acting in a particular role. Obtain the sale record, proceeds accounting, lien history, and governing claim instructions. The former owner is a lead, not proof that no competing interest has priority.

sections.heading: Contracts follow authority, not the investigator's label
paragraphs: A fee agreement must identify the actual service, authorized client, payment source, and event that earns compensation. An individual heir can engage research concerning their own interest without thereby authorizing expenses against an entire estate. A personal representative's engagement raises a separate question: whether that representative can retain the service on the proposed terms and whether payment requires court review. A state claim assistance contract faces its own timing, disclosure, and compensation rules. Calling all three services heir hunting does not harmonize those rules. Misclassification can produce an unenforceable agreement, an invalid assignment, or a demand against someone who never owed the fee. Classify the asset and authority before choosing contractual language or projecting collections.

Use a lane memorandum as the first work product. Record the asset identifier, decedent or reported owner, current custodian, jurisdiction, procedural posture, prospective claimant, and evidence of signing authority. Keep entitlement and contactability in separate fields: a located relative may have no inheritable share, while a well-supported heir may remain difficult to reach. For a probate matter, distinguish letters appointing the representative from a petition merely requesting appointment. For a corporate property claim, distinguish an officer's current position from authority to act for a dissolved predecessor. For surplus, distinguish the auction price from the custodian's confirmed balance. Each distinction prevents a plausible public record from silently becoming an unsupported contractual assumption.

Consider an illustrative file showing a deceased homeowner, a completed trustee sale, and a state listing for an old utility refund. There are at least two assets, potentially two procedures, and possibly an estate proceeding needed to establish who may act. The same death certificate can support both files, but neither an engagement nor an award automatically transfers between them. Build separate asset records linked to one research subject, assign separate deadlines, and document which custodian receives each packet. If the surplus was already distributed, close that opportunity rather than attaching its stale amount to the utility claim. This asset-level discipline makes case economics intelligible and prevents double-counting recoveries in the sales pipeline.

sections.heading: Track 01: Public-Record & API Intelligence
paragraphs: The public_record_api_intelligence play converts permitted public data into a prioritized evidence queue. Inputs include probate docket indexes, appointment entries, recorder instruments, published surplus lists, state property listings, and official business registry records. Supplement with authorized vital records and source-specific exports where access permits; public visibility does not mean unrestricted bulk access or access to sealed attachments. Preserve the source URL, retrieval date, query parameters, record identifier, and a copy or permitted reference to the underlying document. A docket index describes events but may omit the operative order. Treat index-only findings as leads until the document supports them, and separate verified fields from inferred relationships in the case database.

The four-step workflow is acquire, normalize, corroborate, and route. Acquire from documented APIs, downloads, or records requests at the source's allowed pace. Normalize dates, entity suffixes, addresses, and instrument numbers without deleting raw values. Corroborate each promising match against an independent identifier and the document establishing the asset or authority. Route the result to the correct legal lane with an assigned researcher, next evidence request, and explicit rejection reason when unsuitable. A shared surname and city are weak signals; a matching predecessor corporation number and historical address are stronger, but still require successor evidence. Maintain one canonical asset key so repeated downloads do not inflate the inventory or trigger duplicate claimant outreach.

Measure the queue rather than boasting about scraped rows. Record source coverage against the stated jurisdiction list, document retrieval success, duplicate rate, verified claimant yield, median record age, and labor minutes per qualified file. In an illustrative batch of 200 leads, 40 duplicates and 80 obsolete records leave 80 for review; eight supported cases represent a four percent yield on gross intake, not ten percent on all available opportunities. If acquisition and review cost $640, qualified acquisition cost is $80 before deeper genealogy, outreach, and claim preparation. Track those later costs separately. A rising yield can conceal shrinking source coverage, so report both denominators alongside the case count and avoid treating incomplete downloads as empty jurisdictions.

sections.heading: Replace portal fragility with a durable evidence queue
paragraphs: The naive portal-scraping trap begins when an operator equates faster requests with better inventory. HTTP 429 responses and CAPTCHA blocks indicate that the acquisition method has reached an access boundary; retries without a budget can turn one missed update into an entire night's corrupted intake. Do not route around controls with identity rotation or CAPTCHA defeat. Honor documented retry instructions, stop automated access when required, and preserve the last successful snapshot as historical data. Mark freshness explicitly rather than presenting cached records as current balances. Distinguish a transport failure from a genuine zero-result response, and retain response metadata sufficient to explain why a jurisdiction's apparent opportunity count suddenly fell.

The durable fallback is a records-request and cached-queue operating model. Ask the custodian whether a bulk extract, scheduled export, or documented API is available, describing the record fields and date range needed. Use the applicable state public-records process for state or county records; federal FOIA does not govern a county probate office merely because the request concerns public information. Calendar acknowledgment and production milestones under the applicable rules, log fees, and ingest deliveries through the same deduplication path as online records. While waiting, researchers work already acquired cases in priority order, with a fresh custodian check before reliance. Pending requests remain pending inventory, never invented new assets or assumed recoveries.

Close each research cycle with an evidence audit of a small, defined sample. Select both accepted and rejected records, reproduce the match from stored identifiers, and inspect whether the underlying document supports the chosen lane. Count erroneous merges, stale balances, and missing appointment documents separately because each calls for a different repair. An erroneous merge needs entity resolution changes; stale balances need refresh scheduling; missing authority needs a new documentary task. Compare the cost of an official extract with researcher hours lost to unreliable acquisition. The winning operation is not the one collecting the most names. It is the one producing defensible, correctly routed files without letting access failures or speculative family links masquerade as money.

chapters.executive_summary: An attractive balance is not revenue until an entitled claimant can obtain it and an authorized client owes the agreed fee. Separate individual heir engagements, estate genealogy retainers, and state property assistance contracts. Then distinguish gross inventory from distributable residue, and a public listing from an approved claim. Corporate warrant research can produce substantial files, but officer matches, statutory timing, and successor authority determine whether those files are usable. Build economics from verified recovery and collectible compensation, while showing claimants the official route for filing directly without a paid intermediary.

sections.heading: Separate the client, the asset holder, and the person writing the check
paragraphs: An individual heir may hire a researcher under a permitted contingency agreement or assignment concerning that heir's interest. The heir is the client; the estate is not automatically the client, and another heir owes nothing merely because the research benefited the family. Define whether compensation attaches to funds actually received, a permitted assigned interest, or another specified event, and verify that the proposed arrangement is valid in the relevant jurisdiction. An assignment can change rights and collection mechanics, so it is not simply an invoice with a different heading. Identify the signer's capacity and avoid presenting a projected inheritance as cash already available to satisfy a fee. A signed agreement without a collectible recovery remains a contingent business asset.

An estate administrator or other personal representative may instead retain genealogy services to identify beneficiaries or resolve missing branches. Here the engagement concerns work for the estate, usually defined by a research scope, rate or fixed budget, and deliverable. Obtain evidence of appointment and confirm the representative's powers, any restrictions, and the applicable process for payment or court review. A petitioner's promise before appointment is different from an authorized representative's engagement. Separate professional research charges from reimbursable document purchases and identify who approves expanded scope. A well-documented report may be payable under the engagement even if it excludes a suspected heir; the service is evidentiary work, not necessarily a successful percentage recovery for one individual.

For state custodial property, the Controller holds the asset and adjudicates the claim through its procedures, but that does not make the Controller the investigator's customer. The claimant generally establishes identity and entitlement, receives the approved disbursement through the authorized process, and owes any valid assistance fee under the separate agreement. Do not assume the agency will split a payment or honor an assignment without confirming its rules. Give the claimant the official California State Controller unclaimed property search and claim route at claimit.ca.gov, explain that they can file directly without paying a locator, and describe the actual work your fee buys. Keep disclosure distinct from sales pressure: convenience, document assembly, and difficult succession evidence are services, not exclusive access to government money.

sections.heading: Gross inventory is not distributable residue
paragraphs: California Probate Code section 8800 generally requires the personal representative to file an inventory and appraisal within four months after letters are first issued, subject to the court's permitted extension. The inventory is a structured account of estate property and value, not an assurance that heirs receive the headline total. Review the filed Inventory and Appraisal, attachments, supplemental inventories, creditor filings, secured loan statements, tax obligations, and available accountings. Check valuation dates and whether a listed interest is fractional, encumbered, or difficult to sell. A residence valued at $500,000 with a $300,000 mortgage is not $500,000 of heir spending power. Equally, assets passing outside probate should not be added to the probate fee base just because they belonged to the same decedent.

Use an explicit illustrative waterfall: $600,000 of gross probate assets, less $120,000 of secured debt, $40,000 of administration and funeral costs, $60,000 of taxes and other allowed creditor obligations, and a $30,000 reserve leaves $350,000 provisionally available for distribution. These buckets must be mutually exclusive; do not deduct a mortgage twice if a sale schedule already reports net proceeds. The reserve is a planning holdback, not necessarily a final expense. Reconcile each amount to a dated document and label estimates, disputed claims, and settled balances separately. If two heirs share that provisional residue equally, each modeled interest is $175,000, not $300,000. A later tax adjustment or contested claim changes both the residue and the fee opportunity.

A purely illustrative ten percent fee on one heir's $175,000 actual receipt would be $17,500, assuming that arrangement is valid and the contract uses that base. This example does not import the California state-property locator ceiling into probate engagements or establish a permitted probate rate. If the firm spends $4,000 on research and records, its contribution before overhead is $13,500 only after collection; unrecovered files and financing costs still affect portfolio profit. Track expected receipt date separately from amount, because a $17,500 fee collected eighteen months later cannot fund today's payroll. Rebuild the waterfall when property is sold, claims are resolved, or the representative proposes distribution, and do not treat an unsigned draft accounting as a final award.

sections.heading: Track 01: State Treasury Escheatment & Unclaimed Corporate Warrant Recovery
paragraphs: The unclaimed_property_escheatment_arbitrage play targets overlooked corporate property, including uncashed warrants above $25,000 as an internal prioritization screen. In this context a warrant is a government payment instrument, not an equity purchase right or an arrest record. First determine whether the unpaid item remains with the issuing agency, has expired under the issuer's rules, or has actually been remitted into a state custodial property program. Those states lead to different reissue or claim procedures. A stale warrant list is not automatically the Controller's payable inventory. Record issuer, warrant number, payee, issue date, available amount, and current custodian. Where the public record does not reveal the amount, retain it as unknown rather than fabricating a threshold-qualified lead.

Cross-match the payee against Secretary of State records using entity number, jurisdiction, former names, historical addresses, merger records, and filed officer information. A current officer match creates a route for verifying authority; it does not prove personal ownership of corporate funds or authorize payment to that officer. Search beyond active corporations when the payee is dissolved, suspended, merged, or acquired, but document the chain from original payee to current claimant. Request the documents the relevant custodian requires, which may include officer authority, merger evidence, corporate identification, and proof connecting the entity to the reported address. A similarly named active company is not a substitute for a dissolved predecessor unless the succession documents actually connect them.

Build the commercial case only after checking timing and collectibility. For California property covered by CCP section 1582, agreements entered during the interval from the statutory holder report through twelve months after delivery to the Controller are invalid under that section. Outside the prohibited interval, covered agreements still face the ten percent compensation limit and written, signed disclosure requirements. Do not substitute the warrant issue date, database publication date, or first outreach date for the required statutory events. Obtain support for report and delivery dates; hold the contract task when those dates are unknown. Distinguish this agreement restriction from the underlying owner's ability to file a claim, and check other jurisdictions independently rather than exporting California's interval nationwide.

sections.heading: Turn a promising balance into a collectible, documented fee
paragraphs: The naive trap is to treat every large balance as a ready-made ten percent invoice. A $40,000 corporate listing might produce at most $4,000 under an applicable ten percent ceiling, but that arithmetic says nothing about whether the agreement is timely, the entity is entitled, or the Controller approves the full amount. If records and research cost $1,200 and later servicing costs $600, modeled contribution is $2,200 before overhead only on a full, paid recovery. At a fifty percent collection probability across comparable files, expected gross fees are $2,000; subtract the full $1,800 if those costs are incurred on every file, leaving just $200. Label that probability as an assumption unless your own completed cohort supports it.

Use a case ledger that keeps listed amount, verified custodian balance, claimed amount, approved amount, claimant receipt, and firm fee collection as separate fields. Attach the source and date for each transition. A status marked submitted does not justify recognizing an approved balance, and a Controller payment confirmation does not prove that your invoice has been paid. Record why cases fail: wrong entity, missing successor documents, prohibited agreement timing, duplicate recovery, or insufficient remaining balance. Those categories improve screening more than an undifferentiated lost-case count. Measure cycle time from qualified engagement to receipt and track pending cases by age, so a growing queue of unresolved claims is not mistaken for an expanding cash-generating book.

Finish each offer with a concrete scope and the official alternative. Explain which records you obtain, which identity documents the claimant supplies, what triggers compensation, and how unrecovered expenses are handled under the valid agreement. For California covered locator agreements, capture the required written disclosures, including the nature and value of the property and the name and address of the person or entity possessing it, alongside the claimant's signature. Check the current statutory text and custodian instructions before using a template. Never imply a public balance is secret or that an heir or company must hire your firm to approach the agency. The durable service sells documented execution on a difficult file, not ownership of the claimant's access to their own money.

chapters.executive_summary: Heir hunting earns money when documented entitlement produces a recovery and a lawful agreement makes the research fee collectible. A listed estate balance is neither revenue nor an heir's distributable share. Price the correct recovery channel, verify contract timing and fee limits, and charge failed research against successful cases. The illustrative $60,000 recovery produces only $3,000 of contribution after specified direct costs and acquisition allocation. Annual scenarios must then absorb fixed overhead, capacity constraints and collection delays. Keep the official scorecard separate from cash forecasting: attractive annual profit cannot fund tomorrow's record requests without available working capital.

sections.heading: Sell a defined recovery service, not a signature
paragraphs: Begin the commercial file with the asset channel, not the percentage. A California Controller unclaimed-property claim and an inheritance distributed through probate involve different procedures, counterparties and contract restrictions. Record the holder, property identifier, decedent, proposed claimant, approximate recoverable interest and source date before quoting terms. California Code of Civil Procedure section 1582 regulates agreements to locate, deliver, recover or assist in recovering property reported under the unclaimed-property chapter, including a restricted contracting period and a ten-percent ceiling for covered agreements. That ceiling is not a universal probate finder rate, and a percentage below it does not cure defective timing or disclosures. Obtain channel-specific review using the actual agreement and record chronology rather than borrowing a competitor's form.

Define the earning event and the payment event separately. An illustrative agreement can make compensation contingent on the named claimant actually receiving the identified property, with payment due after documented receipt; whether that structure is permitted depends on the governing rules. A database match, signed authorization, filed petition or preliminary entitlement finding should not silently become an invoice trigger. Specify the fee base, treatment of partial distributions, excluded assets, termination and responsibility for approved third-party costs. Identify who receives the funds and avoid assuming the researcher may hold client money. Use a separate engagement where a licensed attorney is needed, and distinguish independent legal services from any prohibited sharing of legal fees with a nonlawyer.

Before execution, reconcile the proposed percentage with the maximum lawful compensation and every associated charge. Calling part of the compensation a document fee or marketing fee does not automatically remove it from a statutory ceiling. Preserve the reviewed version, signature dates, required disclosures and the event evidence supporting eligibility to contract. Explain the claimant's direct recovery route rather than implying a government affiliation or exclusive access to public records. A lawful contract still leaves credit risk: the claimant may dispute the invoice or receive less than the estimated share. Treat enforceability, recovery and collection as separate uncertainties in the case register. The operator's commercial advantage is accurate evidence and efficient service, not a contract that exaggerates entitlement or obscures alternatives.

callout.body: Do not quote a collectible fee until the property channel and contract conditions are established.

sections.heading: Reconcile the complete case waterfall
paragraphs: The worked case starts with $60,000 actually recovered by the client, not the gross face value of an estate. Assume a lawful, enforceable ten-percent contingency agreement for this particular channel. The business receives $6,000 in fees; the other $54,000 is client value, not operating revenue. Deduct $1,200 for certified vital records and genealogy labor, then $800 for independent legal review borne by the business. Deduct another $1,000 allocated from the acquisition cohort, including searches that produced no valid heir, no collectible property or no signed engagement. The remaining $3,000 is contribution before fixed operating expenses and tax. It is neither the founder's take-home cash nor a promise that each completed file will support the same costs.

Use a cohort denominator that cannot improve merely because failed leads disappear from the dashboard. If twenty researched leads consume $4,000 of acquisition effort and only four eventually produce collected fees, allocate $1,000 to each collected case in that cohort. Preserve the original twenty identifiers and explain closures with reasons such as duplicate property, insufficient kinship evidence, superior claimant or uneconomic balance. Do not count the same genealogy hours both inside the $1,200 direct-cost bucket and inside acquisition allocation. Time sheets should distinguish lead screening from accepted-case proof work. If only two cases collect, acquisition burden becomes $2,000 per successful case, reducing the same waterfall contribution to $2,000 before overhead; the recovered principal has not changed, but the economics have.

Maintain a budget, committed-cost total and paid-cost total for every case. A certified certificate ordered today is a commitment even if the card statement has not arrived. Record rebates, refunds and unused retainers against their original cost category, rather than presenting them as new recovery revenue. Track owner research hours at an internal replacement rate so an unpaid founder does not make a labor-intensive file look artificially scalable. For financial reporting, reconcile that management estimate to actual booked expenses instead of deducting fictional payroll twice. Review contribution by recovery channel and acquisition source quarterly. A large payout from one exceptional estate can conceal several years of weak screening, so show both the individual case waterfall and the entire intake cohort's cumulative cash result.

sections.heading: Translate case contribution into annual owner economics
paragraphs: The official Volume 001 scorecard is 87 out of 100, comprising 22, 23, 18, 12 and 12 points, with a plus-or-minus-three-point range and High confidence designation. Its annual operating scenarios appear below without substituting recovered client principal for gross recognized fees. Conservative assumes $80,000 of recognized fees and $20,000 owner net profit at a twenty-five-percent margin. Base Case assumes $340,000 and $127,500 at thirty-seven-and-a-half percent. Scaled Small Team assumes $600,000 and $300,000 at fifty percent. These are planning scenarios, not observed cohort results. The scorecard confidence label describes the assessment, not a statistical probability that a new operator will achieve those earnings. Use the exact scenarios for comparison while replacing their operating assumptions with actual evidence during the pilot.

The implied annual expense budgets are $60,000, $212,500 and $300,000 respectively: subtract owner net profit from gross recognized fees. Each budget must absorb direct delivery costs, unsuccessful acquisition, paid labor, software, insurance and other operating overhead without duplicate allocations. The people counts describe one full-time role plus three contractors in the first two cases and two full-time roles plus four contractors at scale. They do not represent four or six salaried full-time equivalents. Define contractor hours, rates and scopes before deciding whether the expense envelope can support the workload. For this planning presentation, owner net means business operating profit after modeled operating expenses and before the owner's personal income taxes; document owner compensation treatment separately when comparing it with a salaried job.

At an average collected fee of $6,000, the annual fee targets correspond to approximately 13.3, 56.7 and 100 fee-equivalent cases. Those fractions are a throughput comparison, not permission to book an incomplete claim as earned revenue. Real case counts depend on recovery size, lawful pricing and partial receipts. The worked waterfall's fifty-percent contribution rate leaves no fixed-overhead headroom at a fifty-percent annual net margin. Therefore the scaled scenario requires improved contribution economics, such as larger average fees or lower acquisition and delivery cost per dollar, rather than copying the example one hundred times and ignoring overhead. Test that bridge explicitly. Recognition policy also matters: signed contingencies and unresolved claims are pipeline, while recorded revenue must follow the business's documented accounting policy and remain reconcilable to collections.

sections.heading: Stress the calendar before expanding intake
paragraphs: Build separate cash schedules for six, twelve and eighteen months between initial spending and collection. These are probate administration stress windows, not statutory completion deadlines; litigation, missing heirs or asset sales can extend them. California Probate Code section 11420 establishes an order for paying estate debts, including priority for administration expenses. It does not make a private heir-finder invoice a priority estate administration expense merely because the researcher found an heir. Debts, taxes, expenses and competing interests can reduce what is distributable before any contingency fee becomes payable. Review the inventory and appraisal, creditor claims, accountings and distribution orders relevant to the case. Never forecast the fee simply by applying a percentage to the largest asset figure appearing in a docket.

Suppose fixed business cash spending is $2,000 monthly and five accepted cases each require $2,000 of direct spending before collection. With no intervening receipts, required funding is $22,000 for six months, $34,000 for twelve months and $46,000 for eighteen months, before additional acquisition spending or contingency reserves. The $10,000 direct-cost component combines the worked example's records, labor and review costs, but does not include its cohort allocation. Show acquisition cash separately to avoid understating the funding requirement. If all five expected payments slip by six months, fixed spending adds another $12,000. A profitable expected outcome cannot pay vendors during that extension. Calculate the lowest projected cash balance each month rather than relying on an annual profit total that hides the trough.

Close the monthly review by comparing expected receipt dates with documented case events. An administrator's estimated timetable, an unsigned proposed distribution and an entered order are different evidence strengths. Update the forecast when creditor disputes, identity defects or missing certificates arise, and retain the previous estimate to expose repeated optimism. Stop new paid intake when committed costs plus the next operating period exceed available unrestricted cash and the protected reserve. Continue necessary existing obligations through a funded plan rather than abandoning files. Separate business reserves from household living expenses, and never count client funds as working capital. Expansion becomes rational when completed cohorts demonstrate positive contribution, collectible agreements and a cash cycle the business can finance even under the delayed scenario.

chapters.title: Realistic Startup Requirements
chapters.subtitle: A bounded research pilot, professional review and enough cash to wait.
chapters.executive_summary: A $5,000 launch budget can test one research lane, but it cannot finance an open-ended portfolio of delayed probate recoveries. Reserve $1,500 for entity setup, contract review and insurance, $600 for a ninety-day research stack, $900 for certified records and postage, and $2,000 as business cash reserve. Start with defined jurisdictions, reviewed service boundaries and an encrypted case register. Expand only after the pilot supplies evidence about cost, entitlement quality and collection timing. Multi-case operations require a separate working-capital forecast, often modeled at $10,000 to $50,000, with explicit stop rules before spending outruns cash.

sections.heading: Buy a bounded experiment, not a miniature national firm
paragraphs: Define the pilot as ninety days in one recovery lane and a narrow jurisdiction set, with an initial research cohort of twenty leads rather than unlimited intake. The objective is to measure whether reliable entitlement evidence can be assembled within a predetermined cost, not to promise collections during the pilot. Use the $5,000 stack as four separate envelopes: $1,500 for entity formation, contract legal review and errors-and-omissions insurance; $600 for the ninety-day research stack; $900 for certified vital records and postage; and $2,000 of business cash reserve. The arithmetic leaves only $3,000 available for planned deployment. Household living costs, major equipment purchases and contested litigation are outside this example and need their own funding before the founder relies on the business for income.

Get written quotes before treating the $1,500 professional-services envelope as adequate. Entity filing charges, insurance premiums, deductibles and the scope of legal review vary; the allowance does not establish that coverage is available or suitable. Ask whether the proposed policy covers genealogy research, privacy incidents and the actual recovery services, and record exclusions rather than assuming a general policy covers everything. If the necessary review and coverage exceed the envelope, narrow the pilot or increase its funding before commitments. Do not quietly raid the $2,000 reserve to preserve an attractive launch headline. Keep counsel's contract review separate from any later representation of an estate or claimant, which may require a different engagement, client and fee arrangement.

The $600 research envelope equals $200 per month over ninety days, so subscribe only to sources that answer a defined question in the chosen lane. A county probate index, an official property listing and a genealogy database may be useful; five overlapping subscriptions with no measurable retrieval advantage are not. Track subscription renewal dates and export permitted working notes before cancellation. The $900 records envelope averages $45 across twenty leads, but screening should eliminate weak matches before certified orders, leaving more money for the few files that warrant proof. Quote record fees and delivery times individually because death certificates, marriage records and foreign documents differ substantially. Spend on a named evidence gap, not on collecting every available document about a surname.

sections.heading: Confirm the service boundary before client acquisition
paragraphs: Write a one-page service description covering jurisdictions, sources, outreach, deliverables and the party responsible for legal filings. California Business and Professions Code section 6125 generally restricts practicing law in California to active licensees of the State Bar. A researcher can gather and organize historical evidence without assuming authority to advise an heir about contested legal rights or represent them in court. Have counsel identify where the proposed workflow crosses from factual genealogy into legal advice, document preparation or representation. Do not present a researcher as an estate attorney, personal representative or government official. When a matter requires legal work, route it to appropriately qualified counsel under a clear engagement rather than describing the same work as administrative assistance.

Perform a private-investigator licensing pre-check in every jurisdiction where the actual services may trigger regulation. Business formation alone is not a professional license, and public availability of records does not establish a universal exemption. Describe the factual tasks to the relevant licensing authority or local counsel: locating living people, investigating identity, establishing relationships and performing compensated recovery assistance. Record the response, date, scope and any exemptions relied upon. Where licensing or supervision is required, budget for it or exclude the activity from the pilot. Do not treat a subcontractor's credential as automatically covering the business. Confirm the contracted party's permitted role, current status and insurance before sharing a live case or allowing outreach under the firm's name.

For California unclaimed-property work, review Code of Civil Procedure section 1582 before offering an agreement. Its restrictions concern covered property recovery agreements, including timing, compensation limits and required information; they are not a general permission slip for every inheritance engagement. Assemble the property report and transfer chronology needed to assess the restricted period, and have the reviewer specify which event makes contracting permissible in the actual case. A client signature cannot repair a prohibited agreement. For a probate lane, separately review the relevant probate rules and engagement structure rather than importing the unclaimed-property ceiling as universal. The pilot should produce a usable contract checklist tied to the selected lane, with unresolved questions visible before paid acquisition starts and before the first claimant is asked to engage.

sections.heading: Build an encrypted register that can survive handoffs
paragraphs: The minimum case register needs a stable case identifier, source URL or record reference, jurisdiction, property channel, decedent identifiers, potential claimant, relationship hypothesis, evidence status, next action, owner, committed costs and review date. Separate an unverified match from a documented kinship link; an identical name is not identity proof. Store source retrieval dates and document references so another researcher can reproduce the conclusion without repeating every search. Use a dedicated business account and an encrypted document store, with encryption at rest and in transit where supported. Full-disk encryption protects a lost locked device but does not prevent an already authenticated user from opening files. Pair it with access controls, automatic screen locking, updated software and a tested recovery process.

Limit each contractor to assigned case folders and only the documents needed for that task. Use individual accounts, multifactor authentication and prompt access removal when an engagement ends; shared passwords make attribution and revocation unreliable. Keep unnecessary identity numbers out of filenames, chat messages and task-board titles. A register entry can point to a restricted document instead of embedding an entire birth certificate or identity scan. Record who exported or shared a sensitive packet, the recipient and the reason. Before sending, verify the destination using a known contact route and use a restricted transfer mechanism rather than an unrestricted public link. Treat source access terms and record eligibility restrictions as part of the research workflow, especially when requesting certified vital records.

Create encrypted backups on a schedule matched to daily work and keep recovery credentials separate from the device being protected. Test restoration with a synthetic case before collecting sensitive client documents; a green backup icon is not evidence that recovery works. Retain originals and annotate copies so corrections do not erase the source evidence. Adopt a documented retention period based on engagement duties, disputes and applicable requirements rather than accumulating files forever. Log deletion decisions and suspend routine deletion when a relevant preservation obligation exists. If a device is lost or an account appears compromised, revoke access, preserve available logs and assess exposure before resuming sharing. The pilot needs a simple executable procedure, not an expensive security product that nobody has configured or practiced using.

sections.heading: Separate portfolio runway from the pilot and enforce stop rules
paragraphs: A multi-case operation may require $10,000 to $50,000 of working capital, but that range is a scenario input rather than an assurance of sufficient funding. At $2,000 monthly operating expense, those balances cover five to twenty-five months before direct case spending. At $10,000 monthly expense, they cover only one to five months. An eighteen-month wait at the higher burn consumes $180,000 before incremental case costs, well beyond the range. Forecast monthly cash using actual payment dates, contractor commitments, software renewals and record orders, with no receipts until a defensible collection event. Compare six-, twelve- and eighteen-month collection scenarios and a no-collection pilot outcome. Keep owner household reserves separate and exclude client property from available business funds.

Set written stop rules before the first subscription purchase. In this pilot, pause new discretionary spending when deployed costs plus outstanding commitments would exceed $3,000, or when projected unrestricted business cash would fall below the protected $2,000 reserve. Stop adding leads after the initial twenty until the cohort review establishes evidence quality and remaining capacity. Stop paid work on a file when the next research step has no defined evidence question or when the remaining plausible lawful fee cannot cover incremental cost under a conservative outcome. An unresolved licensing issue or an impermissible contracting date stops that affected activity immediately, not unrelated permitted research. These are bounded pilot decisions; they do not cancel existing obligations or justify losing documents, missing agreed notices or abandoning a claimant without an orderly handoff.

Review the cohort at thirty, sixty and ninety days using intake counts, supported relationship chains, rejected matches, committed cost per viable file and documented next events. Do not require ninety-day cash collections from a lane deliberately modeled around longer administration periods, but do require a credible funded continuation plan for accepted cases. At day ninety, cancel nonessential renewals and choose closure, a narrower repeat pilot or a separately financed expansion. Expand only when service permissions are resolved, the evidence process is reproducible and the downside cash forecast remains funded. If the experiment fails, preserve necessary records, settle vendor commitments and explain the evidence-based reason for closure. A stopped $3,000 experiment with its reserve intact is more useful than an expanding pipeline whose apparent asset value never becomes collectible revenue.

chapters.title: What Experienced Operators Know That Beginners Miss
chapters.subtitle: The best early decision is often a documented no-go.
chapters.executive_summary: Experienced heir hunters price the residue, not the headline estate. A valuable house can conceal a mortgage shortfall, unpaid taxes, administration costs, and a Medicaid recovery claim that leaves heirs nothing. This chapter separates statutory payment constraints from an operator's spending rules, then turns both into a staged research process. Spend $25 to establish a credible opening, $150 to test essential records, and $600 on specialist genealogy only when the economics survive. Record every rejection with evidence and a reopening condition so dead leads become reusable intelligence rather than recurring expenses.

sections.heading: Value the distributable residue before valuing the family tree
paragraphs: A probate inventory answers what the estate reports owning; it does not answer what an heir will receive. Start with the filed inventory and appraisal, the latest account, the creditor claims register, and recorded security instruments. Assign an evidence date to every number. A valuation from eighteen months ago is not a current sale estimate, and an original deed of trust is not a current payoff statement. Separate cash already held by the representative from property that must be sold. Mark disputed ownership and inaccessible balances as unresolved rather than silently counting them. The senior operator's first deliverable is a dated residue worksheet with traceable sources, not a polished family tree or an optimistic percentage fee calculation.

Consider an illustrative house appraised at $420,000, with $18,000 of estate cash. A current mortgage payoff of $350,000, $14,000 of property taxes, $29,000 of expected sale expenses, $24,000 of administration costs, and $30,000 of other payable claims produce negative $9,000: $438,000 minus $447,000. Do not present the $438,000 asset total as an heir opportunity. Also do not double count property taxes already included in a payoff or closing estimate. Reconcile each deduction against the underlying statement. A lien that attaches to the house and an unsecured claim against the estate require different treatment; grouping both into a generic debt percentage hides the very information that determines whether further research deserves funding.

Stress the worksheet before purchasing records. Reduce the expected sale price by ten percent, increase carrying costs for six additional months, and reserve for unresolved claims using explicit scenarios rather than invented precision. In the example, a $42,000 price decline alone destroys any thin surplus that a favorable negotiation might have created. An underwater property can still coexist with other distributable assets, so reject the economic thesis only after checking the complete estate rather than the parcel alone. Conversely, a solvent estate does not imply an attractive individual recovery: a $60,000 residue divided among twelve equal heirs leaves $5,000 per heir before any properly agreed service fee. Research effort follows the reachable share, not merely estate solvency.

sections.heading: Read the payment order instead of assuming heirs come first
paragraphs: California Probate Code section 11420 supplies an order for payment of estate debts, beginning with expenses of administration and then obligations secured by a mortgage, deed of trust, or other lien, subject to the statute's treatment of the secured property. Funeral expenses, expenses of last illness, family allowance, wage claims, and general debts occupy subsequent listed classes. Read the entire provision and related rules before assigning a claim to a line. Section 11420 also preserves preferences established by United States or California law. Therefore, a spreadsheet that automatically ranks every tax claim below every ordinary expense is unsafe. The operative question is which enforceable priority applies to this obligation and this asset, not whether the claimant's name sounds important.

Taxes deserve their own evidence lane because a recorded property tax lien, a decedent's income tax obligation, and income tax generated during administration are not interchangeable. Obtain the available tax statements and relevant filed accounts; request clarification through the authorized representative when private information is necessary. Record whether an amount is assessed, estimated, disputed, secured, or already paid. A missing tax return is not evidence of a zero tax liability. Nor does the absence of a claim on an easily searched docket establish that all governmental claims are extinguished. Where payment priority is uncertain, give the representative or retained probate professional the actual documents and reserve the disputed amount until a supported treatment is available.

The practical wipeout often comes from several ordinary items rather than one dramatic creditor. A delayed sale creates insurance, utilities, property preservation, and additional professional work; a contested accounting can extend that delay. The operator should refresh the residue estimate when a material claim arrives, when an appraisal changes, and before committing the next research tranche. Do not treat a filed claim as conclusively allowed or a disputed claim as conclusively worthless. Track its procedural status and the evidence supporting any reserve. If expenses and superior obligations exhaust available assets, a perfectly documented heir still inherits no distributable residue from those assets. That is a commercial no-go, not a failure of genealogical skill, and the file should say so plainly.

sections.heading: Treat Medicaid estate recovery as a specific statutory inquiry
paragraphs: Under 42 U.S.C. section 1396p(b), states must seek specified recovery for certain Medicaid benefits, subject to statutory protections. For individuals aged fifty five or older when assistance was received, the mandatory scope includes nursing facility services, home and community based services, and related hospital and prescription drug services. Federal law permits states to elect broader recovery for other covered assistance, with statutory exclusions, so the phrase all medical bills after fifty five is an unreliable shortcut. A separate recovery category concerns certain permanently institutionalized individuals described in subsection (a)(1)(B); do not collapse that category into the age threshold. Identify the state program, service dates, service category, and applicable state implementation before estimating an estate recovery exposure.

Section 1396p(b)(2) limits when recovery may occur: recovery is permitted only after the death of a surviving spouse, if any, and only when there is no surviving child under twenty one or surviving child who is blind or permanently and totally disabled under the statutory standard. These protections are not equivalent to a discretionary discount negotiated by an heir finder. Establish the relevant family circumstances through appropriate documents without collecting unnecessary medical details. Depending on the applicable state rules and facts, a protection may defer recovery rather than permanently erase every possible obligation. Avoid promising that a surviving spouse always cancels the claim. Certain home recoveries also involve qualifying sibling or caregiver child protections with specific residence requirements that must be checked separately.

The federal provision requires procedures for waiver where recovery would create undue hardship, but an operator cannot grant a waiver or assume one will succeed. Obtain the state's current notice, application instructions, submission deadline, and hardship criteria from its official recovery program. Record whether an application is pending and model both outcomes until a decision arrives. The federal estate definition includes the probate estate and permits states to adopt an expanded definition covering specified nonprobate interests; check what the relevant state actually adopted, including rules tied to death dates. Request an itemized claim or authorized clarification rather than estimating liability from a nursing home's advertised daily rate. Log the recovery issue as unresolved, protected, waived, payable, or disputed only when the documentary record supports that label.

sections.heading: Buy answers in stages and preserve the reason for every stop
paragraphs: Use three incremental research ceilings: $25 for an initial screen, $150 for a vital record check, and $600 for specialist genealogy. These are internal planning amounts, not predictions of county charges or a universal market price. Count paid retrieval, contractor time, and internal labor at a consistent cost basis. The first stage should establish an open matter, a credible asset source, and no obvious residue wipeout. The second should test the weakest essential kinship link, such as whether the apparent sibling is actually the decedent's sibling. The specialist stage should have a written research question, jurisdictions, expected record types, and stopping conditions. Do not spend $600 merely because the preceding $175 now feels too large to abandon.

Suppose a supported $50,000 residue appears available to one reachable heir and an illustrative, locally permissible agreement would produce a $5,000 fee if recovery succeeds. A rough thirty percent joint probability of proving entitlement and collecting yields $1,500 of expected fee revenue before remaining fulfillment costs, overhead, and tax. Spending all $775 would leave only $725 before those further costs; a twenty percent success probability leaves $225. The example is a decision model, not a fee recommendation or measured conversion rate. Test whether a cheaper record can resolve the biggest uncertainty first. If lawful pricing, likely share, or expected work cannot support the next tranche, stop even when the genealogy is intellectually interesting and the contact seems enthusiastic.

Maintain a dead lead log keyed by court, case number, decedent identifier, and discovery date. Use reason codes such as CLOSED_DISTRIBUTED, NO_RESIDUE, REPRESENTED_HEIR, RECORD_PATH_BLOCKED, and CLAIM_UNRESOLVED, with a short factual explanation and a link or reference to the decisive record. Distinguish a permanent rejection from a temporary hold; a pending claim decision merits a dated review trigger, while a final distribution normally does not merit weekly rechecking. Preserve the minimum necessary personal information and keep sensitive supporting documents in restricted storage. Review rejection patterns monthly to improve source selection and screening questions. The objective is not to maximize the number of files opened; it is to avoid buying the same disproven assumption twice while preserving a defensible path to reopen genuinely changed cases.

chapters.title: Finding Your First Qualified Opportunities
chapters.subtitle: A repeatable official-source workflow beats an indiscriminate lead list.
chapters.executive_summary: Qualified opportunities begin with official records and survive four tests: an open matter with a verified custodian balance, a plausible unrepresented heir class, at least $35,000 of estimated net residue, and a documentary proof path within budget. This chapter turns county probate dockets, public administrator inventories, and unknown heirs citations into a repeatable queue. It integrates the probate docket operator play without confusing foreclosure distress with inheritance entitlement. Measure source latency, preserve provenance, investigate exceptions manually, and approach potential heirs with calm, verifiable facts rather than manufactured urgency or implied government authority.

sections.heading: Build an official-source queue with a traceable identity
paragraphs: Choose one county where probate indexes, filed documents, and public administrator information are accessible through official channels. Map the court portal, the public administrator's published inventories or reports, and the office handling document requests. Record access method, publication cadence, available date range, and any charges before collecting leads. Begin with probate petitions, appointment orders, inventories and appraisals, notices of hearing, accounts, and distribution orders. A public administrator's involvement can indicate an estate needing administration, but it does not prove that no heirs exist or that a private operator has authority to act. Keep the raw source title and retrieval date beside each candidate so another researcher can repeat the search without relying on your memory or a commercial aggregator's description.

Use court plus case number as the primary case key, with decedent name, death date when available, and jurisdiction as matching fields. Names alone are insufficient: two estates can share a surname, a middle initial can disappear in an index, and one estate can generate several proceedings. Preserve the official case identifier exactly while maintaining a normalized search version separately. Attach document dates and docket entry references to extracted facts. If a portal returns a search snippet without the underlying filing, label the assertion unconfirmed. Defer sensitive family details until they are necessary to resolve a specific relationship. The output of discovery is a small evidence queue, not a contact database populated with every person whose name resembles the decedent's.

Unknown heirs citations and notices are useful signals because they show an issue being addressed in a proceeding, not because they prove an undiscovered inheritance. Read the document to establish who issued it, what relief is requested, which persons are named, and what date governs the response. Check later entries for amended petitions, appearances, and distribution orders before assuming the situation remains open. Compare public administrator inventories against the court account because publication dates may differ substantially. A county report listing $90,000 of assets from last year can coexist with a current account showing no distributable residue. Where documents cannot be retrieved online, use the clerk's published request process and budget the delay instead of treating a missing download as evidence of a missing heir.

sections.heading: Run the four qualification tests in their economic order
paragraphs: Gate one requires both open status and an active custodian balance. Verify procedural status from the latest docket and identify the representative, public administrator, or other actual holder of assets. Obtain a dated account or a properly authorized balance confirmation; do not solicit private banking credentials or assume the court clerk holds the money. Record the balance date and reconcile subsequent payments. An open case with an exhausted account fails the economic purpose of this test. A valuable but unsold parcel without verified liquid funds remains a separate property research candidate, not a passed cash opportunity. If access restrictions prevent balance confirmation, mark the test pending and specify the exact document or authorized response needed to resolve it.

Gate two asks whether a plausible heir class remains unrepresented in the relevant matter. California Probate Code section 6402 sets the intestate succession order for the portion not passing to a surviving spouse under section 6401, or the entire intestate estate when there is no surviving spouse. Issue, parents, and other relatives appear in a statutory sequence with conditions; a matching surname does not establish rank or entitlement. Check whether a will governs, whether a nearer class exists, and whether identified people already have a representative or an active claim. Gate three then requires at least $35,000 of estimated net residue after known claims and realistic reserves. This internal threshold concerns the estate, so calculate the prospective heir's fraction separately before estimating any potential fee.

Gate four requires a feasible documentary proof path within the staged budget. Draw each necessary parent to child link and assign a proposed record, jurisdiction, access route, expected cost, and delay. Birth, marriage, death, adoption, and court records may establish different facts; a copied online tree is a lead, not a substitute for admissible proof. Suppose a $70,000 supported residue appears divisible between two equal heirs: the candidate's provisional share is $35,000, not $70,000. If one essential foreign record requires costs beyond the remaining $775 plan, the lead does not pass merely because its estate clears the residue floor. Log a pending alternative retrieval path or reject the economics. Reapply earlier tests when new documents reveal nearer relatives, additional claims, or a changed balance.

sections.heading: Integrate the probate docket play without inheriting scraper fragility
paragraphs: Track 01 Operator Play probate_docket_inheritance_arbitrage, titled Probate Docket & Pre-Foreclosure Notice-of-Default Scraping, becomes useful here as an official record change detection workflow. Use permitted feeds, published downloads, or documented search access; keep probate and recorder events in separate queues. A notice of default can flag property distress and a possible threat to estate equity, but it neither establishes a death nor identifies a legal heir. Join that event to an estate only after matching supported owner and parcel identifiers and reviewing title context. Send a reliable match into the residue worksheet as a debt or timing investigation, not as proof of an inheritance. Ambiguous matches stay unmatched until a researcher resolves the identity question.

For each permitted collection run, store the source reference, retrieval timestamp, document identifier, publication date when provided, and an integrity digest if the storage system supports it. Normalize identifiers without destroying the original values. Compare the new record set against the last successful run, queue additions and material changes, and route extraction failures for manual review. Keep the last successful checkpoint when a portal changes or returns an access error. A successful HTTP response containing a login page is not a successful document retrieval. Respect published access restrictions and use an official request or manual review when automated access is unavailable. The durable advantage is reproducible evidence and controlled exceptions, not a higher request rate against a fragile county website.

Measure event to publication latency separately from publication to discovery latency and discovery to qualification latency. A docket filing entered Monday but published Thursday has a source delay that faster polling cannot remove. If publication time is absent, report it as unknown rather than substituting the event date. An illustrative internal target might be discovery within one business day of availability and an initial qualification decision within two business days of discovery; these are planning targets, not observed performance claims. Report median and ninetieth percentile delays alongside sample counts, failed collection runs, and the share of candidates awaiting documents. Recheck a recent overlapping date window after each successful run to catch backdated additions, deduplicate by stable identifiers, and compare occasional manual samples against the automated queue.

sections.heading: Make the first contact verifiable, calm, and economically honest
paragraphs: Contact a potential heir only after the evidence supports a specific relationship hypothesis and the source permits the intended use. Introduce the business by its real name, state that the connection is preliminary, and provide a public case reference that the recipient can independently verify. Explain the service without implying appointment by the court or exclusive access to government funds. A suitable opening says that public probate records suggest a possible family connection and asks whether the person would like the case reference and a written description of the service. Do not assert that money is waiting for them, demand identity documents in the first message, or manufacture a deadline because a sales script performs better under pressure.

Separate open probate work from locating property already delivered to the California State Controller. California Code of Civil Procedure section 1582 governs agreements to locate or recover property within its unclaimed property scope, including a restricted agreement period tied to statutory notice and delivery, a ten percent fee limit for agreements covered by the provision, and written agreement requirements. Those rules are not a universal price schedule for every probate research engagement. Before proposing terms, identify the actual custodian and property regime, check the current statutory text and official instructions, and explain any direct claim route available to the owner. If the record has moved from estate administration to Controller custody, reassess the engagement rather than recycling a probate contract with a different heading.

Use a restrained follow up schedule and stop when the recipient declines or asks for no further contact. Keep a suppression entry sufficient to prevent another researcher from restarting the same approach. Verify identity through proportionate steps only when needed, and move sensitive documents through a suitable private channel rather than public comments or a bulk mailing. Log outreach date, channel, response, and any factual correction supplied by the recipient. Distinguish a refusal from an invalid lead: an heir may be real and simply prefer to proceed independently. At the weekly review, compare official source candidates, four test passes, willing conversations, and documented outcomes. That funnel reveals where research quality fails without treating pressure, repeated messaging, or unsupported entitlement claims as substitutes for a qualified opportunity.

chapters.title: The Complete Operating Process: Genealogical Proof Standard & Per-Stirpes Math
chapters.subtitle: Turn documented family relationships into a reviewable research exhibit.
chapters.executive_summary: A payable heir claim needs more than a plausible family tree. Build a cited proof argument, resolve conflicting identities, and calculate shares under the distribution rule actually governing the estate. This chapter separates genealogical evidence from legal entitlement, works a $180,000 residue through competing representation systems, and tests adoption, nonmarital parentage, and half-blood relationships. It also examines fractional heir-share acquisitions without confusing an estate expectancy with recorded real-property ownership. Use the exhibit, share schedule, and consensual buyout comparison to expose missing links before anyone prices or transfers an interest.

key_metrics.label: Proof elements
key_metrics.note: Research discipline, not automatic court acceptance.

key_metrics.label: Illustrative residue

sections.heading: Build the five-element proof exhibit
paragraphs: Start with an identity question, not a desired beneficiary: was the claimant's mother the same person identified as the decedent's daughter in the probate petition? The Genealogical Proof Standard requires reasonably exhaustive research, complete and accurate source citations, analysis and correlation, resolution of conflicting evidence, and a sound written conclusion. Reasonably exhaustive does not mean purchasing every database subscription. It means identifying the records capable of proving or disproving each relationship and explaining unavailable material. Build a research plan around birth registrations, marriage applications, divorce judgments, death certificates, probate files, census households, and adoption proceedings where accessible. Log unsuccessful searches with jurisdiction, date range, spelling variants, and collection coverage so another researcher can distinguish negative evidence from an incomplete search.

Assign each person a stable identifier and each source a separate identifier. Attach assertions to evidence rather than attaching a whole document to an unqualified family tree. A death certificate may accurately establish death while supplying secondhand parent names from an informant who never met the parents. Record the informant, creation date, record type, image location, and whether the entry is original, derivative, or transcribed. Correlate addresses, occupations, witnesses, siblings, and dates across records. Two people named John Martin in one county are not one person merely because a search engine merged them. Preserve both hypotheses until distinguishing evidence appears. A citation should let a reviewer retrieve the same page, including repository, collection, volume, page, certificate number, and access date.

Write a conflict register before writing the final narrative. If a census implies a 1908 birth and a contemporaneous registration gives 1906, identify the source of each date, assess informant knowledge, and explain why one carries greater weight. Do not silently choose the date that fits the proposed relationship. The written proof argument should state the question, summarize affirmative and negative evidence, resolve material conflicts, and disclose remaining uncertainty. Separate a research conclusion from a court's determination of heirship. Package the narrative with an indexed pedigree, numbered exhibits, missing-record log, and proposed share schedule. A fresh reviewer should be able to reproduce every parent-child edge without calling the original investigator, and should know exactly which unresolved edge prevents a claim from being priced.

sections.heading: Calculate representation without switching algorithms
paragraphs: First determine what property enters the intestate calculation. California Probate Code section 6402 sets an order for property not passing to a surviving spouse under section 6401, or the entire intestate estate if there is no surviving spouse. Do not apply a descendant fraction to gross asset value while ignoring debts, administration expenses, spouse rights, or nonprobate transfers. In this worked example, the confirmed net residue is $180,000 and the decedent had children A, B, and C. A and B survive; C predeceased leaving surviving children C1 and C2. Assume every relationship and survival requirement is established and no other claimant changes the denominator. Three child branches receive one third each, with C's third divided equally between C1 and C2.

Strict per stirpes fixes the initial division at the child generation, preserving each represented child's branch. Modern per capita with representation generally starts at the nearest descendant generation containing a survivor, then distributes deceased members' shares through their branches. California section 240 starts at the nearest generation with living issue, counts living members and deceased members leaving living issue, and recursively allocates each deceased member's share. Per capita at each generation instead combines the shares of deceased members at the chosen generation and divides that pool equally among eligible descendants at the next generation, repeating as needed. Terminology varies across jurisdictions and instruments. Record the operative statutory or testamentary language, not merely a software menu label. The simple A, B, C example produces identical amounts under all three approaches.

Use a second pedigree to expose the difference. All three children are dead. A left living A1 and deceased A2, whose two children survive. B left living B1. C left deceased C1, whose one child survives. Strict per stirpes gives A1 $30,000, A2's children $15,000 each, B1 $60,000, and C1's child $60,000. Modern representation starts with four grandchild slots: A1, A2, B1, C1. A1 and B1 each take $45,000; A2's children split $45,000 and C1's child takes $45,000. Per capita at each generation gives A1 and B1 $45,000 each, then pools the remaining $90,000 for three great-grandchildren at $30,000 each. Check every schedule totals $180,000, retaining exact fractions until the final cent allocation and documenting any rounding adjustment.

sections.heading: Verify legally relevant parentage and collateral relationships
paragraphs: Nonmarital birth is not a reason to erase an otherwise qualifying child from a pedigree. It is a reason to identify the governing parentage rules and the evidence establishing the legal relationship. In California, read sections 6450 through 6453 alongside the applicable family-law provisions and the facts of the case. Obtain birth records, acknowledgments, parentage judgments, and other permitted evidence rather than treating a surname match as proof. A genetic match can support an investigative hypothesis while leaving legal parentage, admissibility, or inheritance conditions unresolved. Record which proposition each document establishes. Distinguish biological relationships from legally recognized parent-child relationships and from household membership. A person described as a son in an obituary may be a stepchild whose inheritance position needs a separate statutory analysis.

Adoption requires dates, orders, and jurisdiction-specific treatment of relationships to both adoptive and natural families. California section 6451 addresses circumstances in which adoption affects succession through a natural parent, including exceptions; a blanket rule that adoption always removes every biological inheritance link will produce errors. Restricted adoption files require an authorized access route, not impersonation or inference from a sealed index entry. Request accessible orders or other appropriate evidence through the representative or counsel. Keep legal names and former names connected with source references, while limiting unnecessary disclosure of sensitive records. Build a timeline showing birth, adoption, marriage, death, and any later adjudication. A timeline often reveals that a rule applied to the wrong event date is responsible for an apparently insoluble contradiction.

Half-blood relationships matter particularly when the search moves from descendants to parents, siblings, and their issue. California section 6406 generally treats relatives of the half blood like relatives of the whole blood in intestate succession, but do not export that rule into a different state's estate. Identify the shared parent and document each sibling's separate parentage rather than assuming a census household proves full siblings. Include predeceased siblings' descendants where the governing priority and representation provisions require them. sections.heading: Fractional Heir-Share Acquisition & Tenancy-in-Common Buyouts
paragraphs: Track 01 Operator Play fractional_heir_share_partition_forcing concerns fractional interests, but the practical transaction must begin by identifying what the seller actually owns. An expected estate distribution, an assignable beneficial interest, and a recorded tenancy-in-common interest are different assets. Trace the probate order, deed, legal description, encumbrances, and ownership fractions before drafting a purchase offer. A genealogical conclusion does not itself convey land. Price the interest against realistic holding costs, title work, taxes, occupancy, and possible sale expenses. If a house is worth $240,000 with $40,000 of debt and estimated $20,000 transaction costs, a one-quarter economic slice of the remaining $180,000 is $45,000 before interest-specific discounts or obligations. That calculation is an underwriting illustration, not proof of a realizable cash exit.

The Uniform Partition of Heirs Property Act changes the expected partition route where enacted and applicable. Verify the state's definition of heirs property, effective provisions, ownership facts, and procedural deadlines. California's partition framework includes appraisal or other authorized valuation procedures, notice, opportunities for eligible cotenants to buy interests of cotenants requesting sale, and consideration of partition in kind before a court-ordered sale under applicable standards. Do not model a forced auction as an automatic outcome. Appraisal objections, buyout elections, funding periods, and the interests eligible for purchase must come from the governing statute and court orders. In California, also check the expanded application under Code of Civil Procedure section 874.313 rather than assuming the original model act's scope controls every tenancy-in-common proceeding.

The forensic question is whether the return comes from a sound consensual purchase or from an imagined ability to pressure relatives into a distressed sale. Document independent valuation, each owner's informed negotiated price, title defects, and payment mechanics. Prefer a consensual co-owner buyout with a title-reviewed deed and escrow instructions identifying releases, taxes, and recording sequence. If owners disagree, model the expense and uncertainty of the available partition process without promising removal of occupants or bypass of statutory buyout rights. Keep legal representation separate from genealogical research services. Stop a closing when the seller cannot establish the transferable interest or a necessary lien release is missing. A smaller negotiated return with a clean conveyance is materially different from a paper spread dependent on an invalid title assumption.

chapters.question_prompt: Q8: Which tools produce authoritative, reproducible heir research?
chapters.title: Tools, Public Databases & Investigative Stack
chapters.subtitle: Choose authoritative records, lawful access, and reproducible source capture.
chapters.executive_summary: Organize investigative tools by evidentiary role rather than subscription price. Official records establish the starting facts; indexed historical collections connect households; licensed tracing and newspaper sources help locate people and test hypotheses. Preserve the original record, retrieval context, and assertion supported by every source. This chapter translates access restrictions into concrete research decisions and follows severed mineral interests from recorded instruments to pooling dockets. Its mineral example separates a deadline-driven opportunity from an unproven title claim, using curative escrow and documented ownership conditions instead of assuming a database match creates a payable interest.

key_metrics.note: Source quality still requires record-level evaluation.
