key_metrics.note: Preserve retrieval history and original bytes.

sections.heading: Use a three-tier stack without confusing leads with proof
paragraphs: Tier 1 consists of official probate dockets, county recorder instruments, and vital registries. Begin with the court case number, decedent's identity, filing jurisdiction, representative, petition, inventory, notices, and distribution orders. A docket entry is an index event, not necessarily the complete filed document; retrieve the underlying petition or order when the assertion depends on its contents. At the recorder, capture instrument number, grantor, grantee, execution and recording dates, legal description, and referenced earlier instruments. At a vital registry, distinguish an index result from an informational copy or certified record and check who can request each. Official provenance does not make every statement true: an informant can still report an incorrect parent, and a petition may contain allegations never adopted by the court.

Tier 2 supplies historical linkage and property discovery through FamilySearch, Ancestry census collections, Social Security Death Index entries, digitized probate packets, and Regrid or DataTree parcel history. Search indexes broadly, then inspect images for household structure, marginal notes, neighbors, and transcription mistakes. A census relationship field can support co-residence and reported kinship without conclusively establishing legal parentage. SSDI coverage is incomplete and varies with source availability; absence does not prove a person is alive. Parcel aggregators are useful for locating assessment identifiers and likely ownership changes, but they do not replace recorded deeds or a title examination. A probate image hosted by a commercial platform remains a reproduction of a court record; preserve that provenance instead of automatically downgrading or upgrading its evidentiary value based on the website.

Tier 3 covers licensed skip-tracing, obituary archives, newspaper collections, and other corroboration used to locate potential claimants. Treat address and telephone matches as contact leads with retrieval dates, not evidence that a person inherited anything. An obituary can reveal married names, relatives, and migration paths, but family submissions may omit estranged relatives or use social relationships loosely. Confirm the relationship with stronger records before presenting a share schedule. Compare the cost of each query with its expected information value: spending $40 on a decisive court packet can outperform ten inexpensive searches repeating the same unsupported address. Maintain a source-purpose matrix so the investigator knows whether a tool is being used to discover a record, establish an event, corroborate an identity, or find a contact channel.

sections.heading: Make every useful search reproducible
paragraphs: Give every captured source a stable identifier such as HH001-S0042, linked to the case and relevant person IDs. The source log should record repository, collection, jurisdiction, case or instrument number, document date, page range, retrieval timestamp with timezone, query terms, filters, and access method. Save the original permitted download before making annotations or OCR derivatives. Record a SHA-256 digest of the saved bytes and preserve the filename and media type. A hash can demonstrate that your saved file has not changed; it cannot prove the repository was accurate or that the document is genuine. For dynamically rendered pages, preserve a permitted page capture and the retrieval context, since a search URL alone may expire or reproduce a different result tomorrow.

Separate source records from assertions. A single marriage application may support a date, prior surname, age, and parental identity with different confidence levels. Create an assertion entry containing subject ID, predicate, proposed value, source ID, exact page or image reference, transcription, and analyst interpretation. Preserve the distinction between what the record says and what the investigator infers. When two sources conflict, retain both assertions and attach a resolution note rather than overwriting the older value. Track image derivatives back to the original bytes, including OCR software output and manual corrections. If access terms prevent storing a full image, record the allowed citation and retrieval path, plus the storage restriction, instead of quietly copying prohibited material into the shared case folder.

Negative searches deserve the same discipline. Record that the county birth index was searched for three spellings from 1900 through 1910 and note whether the collection excludes delayed registrations or certain districts. This supports a bounded conclusion about the search, not a claim that no birth occurred. Use a second reviewer to retrieve one decisive record from the citation alone and to reproduce one negative search with the documented filters. A failure points to missing collection names, unstable links, or ambiguous page numbering. Restrict shared working copies to the data needed for the assignment and keep contact details separate from broadly circulated proof exhibits. Before delivery, reconcile all cited source IDs, flag unavailable attachments, and preserve a versioned manifest identifying the exact exhibit set reviewed.

sections.heading: Match the access route to the actual permitted purpose
paragraphs: The Driver's Privacy Protection Act, 18 U.S.C. section 2721, restricts disclosure of personal information from state motor vehicle records subject to enumerated exceptions. An heir research business does not gain blanket access because its work is useful or because a database vendor accepts payment. Identify the actual statutory basis and verify that the proposed use fits it. The litigation-related exception requires the appropriate connection to a proceeding or qualifying investigation, not a decorative case label added to an unrelated marketing search. The licensed private investigative agency exception ties permitted use to purposes allowed under the statute; a license is not an unrestricted pass. Highly restricted personal information has narrower treatment. Keep the vendor's permitted-use certification and the factual basis for the specific search together.

Section 2721 also addresses authorized recipients' resale and redisclosure, including recordkeeping requirements that can apply to redisclosures. Do not assume that information lawfully obtained for one purpose may be placed in a general prospecting list or handed to an unrelated buyer. Map the data's source, permitted purpose, recipient, and planned disclosure before using motor vehicle information to contact an alleged heir. Where the proposed purpose does not fit an available exception, use public probate notices, authorized vital-record requests, voluntarily supplied documents, or other lawful sources instead. Vendor marketing phrases such as public data or investigator grade do not settle the statutory question. Capture the precise product and source restrictions because a single search service may mix unrestricted public records with restricted datasets in one interface.

The Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, 18 U.S.C. section 1030, addresses specified unauthorized computer access and related conduct; it is not a general declaration that every terms-of-service dispute is a federal crime. Access analysis depends on the system, credentials, restrictions, conduct, and governing case law. Use accounts issued to the authorized researcher, approved export functions, and the repository's available public or licensed access routes. Do not bypass authentication, enter restricted accounts, reuse someone else's credentials, or defeat a denial to obtain records. Rate limits and licensing terms also matter operationally even when they do not independently determine CFAA liability. When a download is unavailable, request records from the clerk or repository rather than treating a technical obstacle as permission to circumvent it. Log the alternative route so the exhibit remains reproducible.

sections.heading: Forced-Pooling Docket & Non-Consent Mineral Lease Curve-Jumping
paragraphs: Track 01 Operator Play forced_pooling_mineral_lease_curve_jumping traces missing mineral owners before state oil and gas commission pooling deadlines. The opportunity starts with a recorded severance: surface ownership and mineral ownership may have followed different chains for decades. Search deeds, mineral reservations, assignments, probate distributions, royalty instruments, and relevant court records using the tract's legal description, not merely a street address or assessor parcel. Compare those instruments with the pooling application, respondent list, notice documents, hearing calendar, and eventual order. A respondent list identifies parties the applicant believes may have interests; it is not a title opinion or an adjudicated heirship schedule. Match names through documented family relationships and trace each transfer until the claimed fractional mineral ownership has a supported chain.

Pooling procedures, election options, notice standards, and consequences of non-consent vary by state and by order. Oklahoma's forced-pooling framework under title 52, section 87.1 is one example, not a nationwide template. Extract the specific election period, payment terms, alternatives, and default consequence from the controlling order and applicable rules. Record the triggering event and actual calendar deadline rather than assuming every state gives the same number of days after a hearing. Locate heirs early enough to obtain documents and independent review, but do not promise that an assignment restarts a deadline or cures defective notice. Verify whether a proposed transaction concerns an unleased mineral interest, a royalty interest, lease rights, or a working interest; their costs, election rights, and exposure are materially different.

For an illustrative tract, assume the decedent owned eight net mineral acres and a verified heir takes one quarter, yielding two net mineral acres. A hypothetical $1,500 per net mineral acre bonus suggests $3,000 gross before deductions, but only if title, lease terms, acreage, and the available election actually support it. An unreleased prior lease, omitted probate, ambiguous reservation, or competing heir can eliminate that expected payment. The curative escrow fallback specifies the required instruments, who obtains them, escrow funding and release conditions, a cure deadline, and what happens if the defects remain. It does not itself extend a commission deadline or establish ownership. Separate any time-sensitive authorized election from the contingent purchase closing. Preserve the docket order and title exceptions together so a buyer cannot mistake deadline urgency for evidence of a transferable interest.

chapters.title: Ethical Outreach, Contracting & Jurisdictional Restrictions
chapters.subtitle: Separate probate assignments, unclaimed-property recovery, licensing, and legal representation.
chapters.executive_summary: Heir outreach works when the recipient can independently verify the estate, the sender, and the proposed service. First classify the asset: a probate distribution assignment is not the same transaction as a state unclaimed-property recovery agreement. Then separate investigative licensing, contract enforceability, and legal representation. This chapter compares four jurisdictions, builds a low-pressure contact sequence, and dissects outbound shortcuts that create avoidable exposure. The operating objective is a documented introduction and a narrow, understandable agreement, not a signature obtained through confusion about government authority, deadlines, or the heir's ability to proceed independently.

sections.heading: Classify the transaction before comparing percentages
paragraphs: Start every intake with four distinct fields: asset custodian, estate venue, recipient location, and proposed service. A county probate estate holding sale proceeds is not automatically a state unclaimed-property account merely because an heir is missing. Obtain the petition, docket number, personal representative's identity, and latest accounting before describing any available inheritance. If a state administrator holds the asset instead, record the property identifier and claim procedure. Keep the two records separate when an estate also owns abandoned funds. A contract drafted for locating a state-held account can fail when reused as an assignment of an expected probate distribution, even when both engagements involve the same family and the same researcher.

California Probate Code Section 11604.5 provides a specific court-review framework for transfers or agreements involving an heir hunter and a beneficiary's distribution. Treat court scrutiny, disclosure, and possible reduction of compensation as central economic variables, rather than assuming a signed assignment controls payment. Florida Section 717.135 addresses agreements to recover property under its unclaimed-property chapter, including prescribed disclosures and compensation restrictions; registration must also be checked under Section 717.1400. Its ordinary fee-and-cost limitation is 20 percent, with statutory alternative disclosure provisions requiring careful review. Do not transplant that percentage into a Florida probate retainer. Record the exact statutory route and form version selected by counsel before presenting a price to an owner.

Texas Property Code Section 74.507 limits covered recovery compensation to 10 percent of the recoverable property's value and imposes enforceability conditions, including a restriction tied to the period after delivery to the comptroller. A compliant percentage alone therefore does not establish a collectible contract. New York SCPA Section 2225 concerns proceedings involving unknown distributees and relevant proof; use it to frame the kinship investigation, not as a universal percentage schedule. Court review of compensation and assignments requires examination of additional authority, including SCPA Section 2112 where applicable. Across all four states, ask counsel to identify the controlling asset regime, timing restrictions, required signatures, review procedure, and fee base in a written file note.

sections.heading: Separate investigation, contracting, and legal representation
paragraphs: A genealogy label does not decide whether paid investigative work requires a license. California Business and Professions Code Section 7521 defines private-investigator activities broadly enough that locating people or investigating identity for compensation deserves a specific licensing analysis. Florida Chapter 493 likewise regulates private investigative services, subject to definitions and exemptions that must actually fit the engagement. Map the acts performed, where personnel work, where subjects are contacted, and which entity invoices the client. Do not infer reciprocity from holding one state's credential. If an exemption is asserted, retain its text and the factual explanation; a trade association membership or a database subscription is not a substitute for a statutory license or exemption.

The research team can assemble birth certificates, marriage records, death records, census extracts, and a source-linked family tree. It should not turn an unresolved relationship into a legal entitlement opinion. Counsel decides how adoption, nonmarital parentage, disclaimers, survivorship, and competing claims affect distribution in the actual venue. Researchers must not hold themselves out as the recipient's lawyer, choose pleadings for an unrepresented heir, or negotiate contested legal rights as though a recovery contract confers a law license. Establish a handoff record identifying the question, supporting documents, missing evidence, and intended attorney recipient. Keep client representation, estate representation, and the research firm's own contract advice distinct, because those interests can diverge sharply during a dispute.

Draft the commercial scope in plain language: what records will be obtained, what deliverables the heir receives, when payment becomes due, and which expenses are included. Distinguish a service contract from a transfer of distribution rights; do not hide an assignment inside a routine authorization. Specify the fee base using a worked dollar example and identify who bears unsuccessful research costs. Avoid blanket powers of attorney and promises that a clerk will release money immediately. Give the recipient a copy before signature, time to consult independent counsel, and a working cancellation or termination contact. Preserve versions and delivery dates so later review can reconstruct what was offered rather than relying on a salesperson's recollection.

sections.heading: Make first contact independently verifiable
paragraphs: Use a short introductory letter that identifies the private firm, the research purpose, and an independent verification path. A usable script reads: We are a private genealogical research firm reviewing public records associated with an estate in this county. Those records suggest you may be a relative; we have not established your entitlement. You can verify the case through the court's independently published contact details. You do not need to send identification or sign an agreement to ask who we are. If you prefer no further contact, tell us through the enclosed contact options. Insert only verified facts, and avoid placing sensitive family relationships or an estimated payout on the outside of the envelope.

For a returned call, first confirm that the person intended to reach your firm without asking them to recite a Social Security number or bank credentials. Explain how the address was sourced and offer to send the public case reference in writing. State that the recipient can contact the personal representative or consult an attorney independently; do not imply your firm exclusively controls access to a public process. If identity documentation becomes necessary, explain the purpose, recipient, secure transfer method, and retention period before collecting it. A callback number printed in your letter verifies only that someone controls that number; it does not independently establish the estate, the research firm's identity, or the recipient's inheritance.

Use certified delivery when a documented delivery attempt is useful, not as a theatrical demand for action. A signature shows delivery activity, not understanding, consent, heirship, or acceptance of a contract. Maintain a contact ledger with source, date, channel, recipient response, and suppression status. A practical internal cadence is one introduction and one measured follow-up unless the recipient requests continued discussion; this is an operating limit, not a statutory safe harbor. Stop after refusal, investigate returned mail, and do not escalate to relatives or employers to pressure a response. Attorney corroboration should mean an accurately described attorney has reviewed the relevant facts or agreed to confirm a limited point, not an unauthorized endorsement pasted onto stationery.

sections.heading: Track 02 Grey-Zone Outbound Forensic Teardown
paragraphs: Treat aggressive outbound proposals as failure analyses, not growth recipes. A vendor offering thousands of cold texts cannot establish lawful outreach merely by saying that all numbers came from public records. The TCPA, 47 U.S.C. Section 227, can expose covered violations to actual loss or statutory damages of $500, with potential enhancement up to three times for knowing or willful violations. Applicability depends on the communication, technology, consent, and other facts; not every unsolicited message produces the same claim. A planning example of twenty separately actionable violations produces $10,000 at the statutory amount before possible enhancement, defense costs, or other claims. That exposure can exceed the entire expected fee from a modest estate lead.

Pretexting creates a different evidentiary failure: the firm obtains attention by misrepresenting its identity or purpose, then must defend a contract built on that interaction. Never impersonate court staff, an estate administrator, a bank, or a family member to obtain records or a signature. Government-lookalike mail is also a poor substitute for a verified source. Section 3001 of Title 39 addresses nonmailable matter and includes conditions concerning solicitations that imply a federal connection; related fraud and deceptive-practice rules may apply beyond that specific provision. Do not reduce the rule to a claim that every official-looking envelope violates one subsection. Analyze the actual representation while choosing plainly private stationery that does not borrow official authority.

The fallback is slower per contact but cleaner per completed matter: a narrowly addressed packet, a truthful explanation, an independently checkable case reference, and counsel corroboration limited to what counsel actually reviewed. Compare channels on collected contribution rather than reply rate. Track verified recipients, requested callbacks, signed agreements, approved compensation, paid fees, and complaints separately. A reply gained through confusion is not a qualified client. Before purchasing an outbound service, require sample messages and provenance records rather than accepting a conversion screenshot. Reject vendors that cannot explain recipient selection or honor suppression. Preserve the final approved wording with the case file so the outreach record and the eventual contract tell the same factual story.

chapters.subtitle: Use bounded collection and evidence-linked triage with human approval gates.
chapters.executive_summary: Automate repetitive collection and document routing while reserving identity, inheritance, outreach, and contracting decisions for people. A useful pipeline preserves original bytes, links every extracted assertion to a page, and treats docket content as evidence rather than executable instructions. The worked case follows a $180,000 net intestate residue through represented shares, a $9,000 fee, and $4,700 of direct costs. Its $4,300 contribution is attractive only if the fee is enforceable and collected. A zero-collection case loses the entire direct-cost budget, so automation should improve selection and traceability rather than merely increase lead volume.

sections.heading: Collect fewer documents with a better receipt
paragraphs: Start with a published court feed, authorized export, or permitted public endpoint rather than a browser session that happens to expose a document. Record the source's access terms, relevant account permissions, request limits, and document categories allowed for collection. Section 1030 of Title 18 addresses unauthorized computer access and related conduct; public visibility is not a universal authorization to defeat access controls. Do not bypass authentication, CAPTCHAs, sealed-record restrictions, or technical blocks. A terms dispute and a federal computer offense are not automatically equivalent, but neither ambiguity nor commercial value justifies evading a denial. Where automated collection is unsupported, use a permitted manual retrieval process and retain the same provenance fields as the feed collector.

Set conservative limits per host and keep them configurable: one request at a time and a five-second minimum interval can be an initial internal budget, not a claim about what any court permits. Honor stricter published limits and Retry-After instructions. On repeated 429 responses, stop the job and record the deferred items; on 401 or 403 responses, stop instead of rotating identities or proxies. Use conditional retrieval where supported, bounded timeouts, capped retries with backoff, and a daily document budget. Persist a checkpoint only after the downloaded object and its manifest entry are durable. That sequence prevents a transient failure from silently advancing the cursor past a petition that the research team never actually received.

Compute SHA-256 over the original response bytes before OCR or normalization. Store that digest with source URL, retrieval time in UTC, case number, docket entry identifier, media type, byte count, and collector version. Preserve the original object as read-only evidence and generate derived text under a separate identifier linked to the original hash. A matching digest demonstrates byte identity, not authenticity, completeness, or truth; compare the document with the official docket when those questions matter. If a court replaces a PDF at the same address, retain both versions and flag the change instead of overwriting history. Restrict access to sensitive documents and record any deletion required by the retention policy without pretending a deleted object remains reproducible.

sections.heading: Page-linked OCR and citation-locked extraction
paragraphs: Render each petition or handwritten will into ordered page images while preserving the PDF's original page index. Record both the machine index and any printed page label, because exhibits often restart numbering. OCR output should carry document hash, page index, bounding box when available, engine version, and a review state for each extracted field. Handwritten dates, crossed-out names, marginal additions, and faint signatures need visual comparison rather than confident reconstruction. A name that resembles two alternatives remains unresolved until another record supports the reading. Retain the uncertain transcription alongside the image rather than replacing it with a plausible surname. The purpose of OCR is to shorten navigation and search, not manufacture a clean evidentiary record from an ambiguous original.

Pass the extraction model only the bounded text and page references needed for the selected task. Require structured fields for asserted name, relationship, date, source hash, page index, exact supporting quotation, and uncertainty. Missing evidence must yield an explicit unknown value, not an inferred answer. Validate that the quoted text occurs in the cited page's extracted text and then have a researcher compare legally significant assertions with the page image. Text matching alone can validate an OCR error perfectly. Never treat a model confidence score as a probability that the inheritance relationship is correct. Link each proposed family-tree edge to its evidence and retain contradictory records so a fluent summary cannot erase the disagreement from the case file.

Docket PDFs are untrusted input, even when downloaded from a genuine court site. A filing can contain adversarial instructions, embedded links, or text that tells a model to ignore prior requirements and send information elsewhere. Treat all such material as quoted document content, never as authority to change the task. Run extraction without email, texting, contracting, payment, shell, or unrestricted network tools. Document links must not trigger automatic retrieval outside the allowlisted collection process. Use strict output validation and reject unexpected keys or executable payloads. A human reviewer approves any subsequent use in correspondence or contract preparation. The system has zero autonomous outreach or contract authority, and that boundary must be enforced by available capabilities rather than a polite instruction alone.

callout.body: No source page, no promoted assertion. A citation is necessary but does not replace checking the underlying record.

sections.heading: Worked case: from estate residue to collected fee
paragraphs: Assume a reviewed intestacy scenario with no surviving spouse, three child branches, and a $180,000 net distributable residue after estate debts, taxes, and administration expenses. Child A and Child B survive. Child C predeceased the decedent and left two surviving children, Grandchild C1 and Grandchild C2. Assume the applicable succession rule divides this estate into three equal child branches and divides Child C's branch equally between those two grandchildren. Counsel must confirm those assumptions, including survivorship and any adoption or disclaimer issues; they are not consequences of the arithmetic alone. The resulting shares are $60,000 for Child A, $60,000 for Child B, and $30,000 for each grandchild. These four shares reconcile to the full $180,000 residue.

The research firm represents only Child A and Grandchild C1 under separately reviewed agreements. Its fee base is therefore $60,000 plus $30,000, or $90,000, not the entire estate. At an assumed enforceable 10 percent fee, Child A contributes $6,000 and Grandchild C1 contributes $3,000, producing $9,000 of collected revenue. Their distributions after those fees are $54,000 and $27,000 respectively, before any other individually applicable costs. Neither Child B nor Grandchild C2 owes the firm money merely because its investigation established the complete family tree. If the proceeding is in California, evaluate the actual agreement under Probate Code Section 11604.5; a 10 percent price is a modeling assumption, not an automatic exemption from court review or a universally permissible rate.

Build the file in dependency order: docket and accounting review establish the residue, vital records establish the branches, counsel checks entitlement and contract treatment, and verified outreach reaches the intended beneficiaries. The worked budget allocates sixty research hours at $45 per hour, or $2,700; $500 for vital records; $1,200 for probate counsel review; and $300 for outreach. Total direct costs are $4,700. Allocate every invoice once, and do not quietly add the same counsel charge to both estate expenses and this firm's operating budget. Here the estate residue is already net and the counsel review is a separate firm expense. The accounting boundary matters because double counting can distort both the heirs' projected distributions and the operator's apparent profitability.

sections.heading: Use contribution, delay, and loss to control the queue
paragraphs: The successful case yields $4,300 contribution, calculated as $9,000 collected fees less $4,700 direct costs. Dividing contribution by collected fees gives 47.777 percent, rounded to 47.8 percent. This is not the firm's net profit margin: rent, general subscriptions, unallocated supervision, owner compensation, financing, and taxes remain outside the case calculation. Conversely, the zero-collection stress test assumes all four direct-cost categories have already been incurred and no fee is recovered, producing a loss of $4,700. Record work in progress separately from cash receipts. A signed contract or a proposed distribution should not be counted as collected revenue merely because an internal dashboard marks the relationship as confirmed or the petition as filed.

Under a deliberately simplified binary model, expected contribution equals the probability of collecting the full $9,000 multiplied by $9,000, minus the certain $4,700 cost. Break-even collection probability is therefore $4,700 divided by $9,000, or approximately 52.2 percent, before overhead and the time value of money. At 70 percent assumed collection probability, expected contribution is $1,600, not $4,300. This sensitivity is a decision aid, not an empirically measured success rate. Court reductions, partial distributions, record delays, disputes, and extra legal work create additional outcomes that the binary model omits. Replace hypothetical probabilities with cohort evidence when enough comparable closed cases exist, while keeping unresolved cases visible to avoid survivorship bias.

Assign a researcher to source acquisition and kinship evidence, an authorized reviewer to contract and entitlement questions, and a named operator to case spending and contact release. One person may fill several operational roles, but the record should still show which decision was made and on what evidence. Review spending after the initial docket review, after essential vital records arrive, and before expensive unresolved branches consume the remaining budget. Automation earns its place when it reduces duplicate retrieval, locates supporting pages faster, or exposes a weak case earlier. Do not assume fewer transcription minutes automatically lower the sixty-hour budget. Measure actual time saved, deduct review and correction time, and update future case estimates only when completed work supports the change.

Budget the -$4,700 zero-collection outcome.

chapters.question_prompt: Q11: How do you scale a small heir-hunting firm without losing control?
chapters.title: Small-Team Scaling: Running a High-Margin 2-to-4 Person Firm
chapters.subtitle: Design for disciplined contribution margins, not guaranteed profitability.
chapters.executive_summary: Scale the work system before expanding the payroll. A lean heir-hunting practice needs separate responsibility for research, independent review, client communication, and legal decisions even when several roles are fractional. This chapter translates those responsibilities into weekly capacity limits, controlled access to sensitive records, and cohort accounting that separates signed opportunities from collected fees. The illustrative portfolio scenarios show why four contributors can still produce only modest owner income, and why the scaled six-person configuration is an expansion beyond the lean core rather than evidence that headcount automatically creates profit.

sections.heading: Separate decisions even when people wear multiple hats
paragraphs: Build the firm around five responsibilities, not five full salaries. The Principal or Case Lead chooses jurisdictions, owns the acquisition budget, resolves scheduling conflicts, and authorizes commercially sensible work. The Senior Genealogist constructs the lineage hypothesis, searches original records, and writes the proof argument. The Independent QC Reviewer tests that argument against conflicting evidence without being its author. The Client and Records Coordinator tracks certified copies, appointments, correspondence, and deadlines. Independent Outside Probate Counsel determines the legal route and handles reserved legal work under a separate engagement. A two-person core can combine principal and coordination duties while buying bounded research and independent review assignments; it cannot make independence real merely by changing an employee's title.

Create a responsibility sheet for every accepted case before ordering expensive records. Record the case lead, researcher, reviewer, coordinator, and counsel contact, plus who may change each deliverable. The researcher may correct a source transcription but cannot mark their own proof packet independently reviewed. The coordinator may send an approved factual status update but cannot improvise an interpretation of intestacy law. Counsel should receive the disputed relationship and governing facts, not a vague request to bless the entire business. When the principal also researches, assign another qualified person to QC and preserve the reviewer's unresolved objections. A revenue target must never silently convert an unresolved parentage conflict into a confirmed heir relationship.

Use a written handoff rather than a meeting as the unit of progress. A research handoff includes the source register, image references, identity timeline, negative searches, conflicting evidence, and proposed next action. QC returns a dated disposition of pass, correction required, or hold, with specific record references. The coordinator then knows whether outreach can proceed or whether another death certificate is needed. If an independent reviewer is unavailable, pause that transition while research continues on another permitted file. Outsourced counsel and reviewers need realistic turnaround expectations; buying ten hours of specialist time does not reserve unlimited availability. Maintain a second qualified supplier for continuity, with a separate confidentiality agreement and scoped access rather than shared passwords.

sections.heading: Turn available hours into a defensible WIP limit
paragraphs: Start with forty protected research hours per week across the team, after subtracting intake, administration, training, and leave. If an active dossier consumes ten research hours each week, the deep-work limit is forty divided by ten, or four concurrent files. This is a concurrency limit, not a promise to finish four cases every week. A dossier requiring thirty total research hours may occupy a slot across three weeks. If all files had that same demand and records arrived instantly, theoretical throughput would be forty divided by thirty, approximately 1.33 research completions weekly. Real throughput is lower when dependencies, corrections, and uneven case difficulty intervene. Distinguish deep research from waiting on certified records so the board represents actual labor commitments.

Run the weekly board with explicit queues: screened intake, active research, external wait, QC, counsel query, outreach, claim pending, and closed. Every external-wait file carries its next follow-up date and an owner; otherwise apparent spare capacity hides abandoned work. Four active files already consume the full forty-hour research budget, leaving no research buffer. A prudent starting schedule assigns three full slots and retains ten hours for correction work or urgent documentary discoveries. If the reviewer has six hours available and each packet needs three, QC can accept two packets weekly, regardless of how quickly researchers draft them. Reduce upstream starts when finished packets accumulate; hiring another researcher does not repair a reviewer bottleneck.

Measure age and effort separately. A claim waiting sixty days for a court event might have consumed only twelve staff hours, while a five-day identity puzzle can consume twenty. Record both on the case board so an old case is not automatically labeled inefficient and a young case is not automatically cheap. Set a research spending checkpoint before the next record order: compare remaining evidence gaps, expected collectible fee, estimated additional labor, and the probability of a legally viable claim. A file that has exhausted its experiment budget returns to the principal for a documented continue, narrow, or close decision. Do not keep every weak lead alive merely to make the pipeline look full; stale WIP makes reliable promises impossible.

sections.heading: Classify workers by facts and restrict sensitive records
paragraphs: Do not treat the letter C in a staffing model as a legal classification decision. Section 203 of Title 29 defines terms including employer, employee, and employ, with employ including suffer or permit to work; it does not make a contractor invoice dispositive. Actual worker status depends on applicable law and the working relationship, with state rules potentially adding different tests. Have the appropriate adviser evaluate control, economic dependence, scheduling, equipment, and the actual services before using a contractor arrangement. Maintain the resulting rationale and revisit it when an occasional researcher becomes a continuously supervised team member. Budget payroll taxes, insurance, and other employment costs when required rather than preserving a fictional margin through a label.

California Business and Professions Code section 7521 describes private-investigator activity broadly enough that compensated locating and investigative work requires a careful scope analysis. Read that provision with applicable exemptions and licensing requirements rather than assuming genealogical branding removes the issue. Send counsel the actual workflow: which persons are located, what records are gathered, who pays, and what communications are made. Counsel should identify which tasks may be performed, by whom, and under which authority in the selected jurisdiction. Outside probate counsel does not automatically supply the firm's separate investigative licensing authority. Keep professional legal work separate from factual research, and stop expansion into a new state until its relevant operating requirements have been evaluated.

Use individual accounts, multifactor authentication, and an encrypted case vault with access granted by case and role. The coordinator generally needs mailing details and request status, not unrestricted access to every identity document. A reviewer needs the evidence packet and source images but not unrelated client payment information. Give outside counsel a scoped transfer or folder rather than a reusable team login. Log exports, expire temporary access, and remove departing contributors promptly. Define retention periods by record type and applicable obligations, with documented exceptions for active disputes. Store redacted working copies where full identifiers are unnecessary; preserve originals in a restricted location. Test recovery from backup with a dummy case before depending on the vault for live work.

sections.heading: Scale collected contribution, not signed face value
paragraphs: Treat the portfolio scenarios as annual planning illustrations, not observed outcomes or staffing prescriptions. Conservative uses one full-time contributor plus three contractors, four people in total, with eighty thousand dollars gross and twenty thousand owner net at twenty-five percent. Base keeps that four-person configuration and models three hundred forty thousand gross with one hundred twenty-seven thousand five hundred owner net at thirty-seven point five percent. Scaled uses two full-time contributors plus four contractors, six people, with six hundred thousand gross and three hundred thousand owner net at fifty percent. That six-person case extends beyond the lean two-to-four-person core. Contractor counts indicate contributors, not full-time equivalents, and each scenario needs its own hours and compensation assumptions.

Reconcile each scenario to its implied cost envelope before discussing growth. Conservative leaves sixty thousand dollars for modeled expenses, Base leaves two hundred twelve thousand five hundred, and Scaled leaves three hundred thousand. Those envelopes must cover the costs included in the model: labor, record procurement, specialist review, counsel paid by the firm, insurance, software, acquisition, and overhead. Define owner net consistently as modeled pre-personal-tax residual after listed business expenses, and disclose whether owner labor compensation is included or excluded. If excluded, track owner hours and an imputed market wage separately. A twenty-thousand-dollar residual supporting full-time owner effort is not evidence of a strong economic wage, even if the nominal percentage margin looks attractive.

Group files by intake month and legal lane, then track screened leads, accepted cases, labor hours, cash outlay, signed fee exposure, claims submitted, fees collected, refunds, and write-offs. Keep signed contingent fees separate from receipts; a large estate value is neither company revenue nor cash available for payroll. For an illustrative cohort collecting thirty thousand dollars against twelve thousand direct costs, contribution is eighteen thousand before overhead and owner labor adjustments. Allocate six thousand of overhead and the remaining twelve thousand is a cohort residual, not necessarily cash in the same month. Include failed files in the denominator. Expand only when matured cohorts support the additional fixed commitment and cash reserves can absorb the zero-collection downside while pending matters remain unresolved.

chapters.question_prompt: Q12: What should you execute during the first thirty days?
chapters.title: The First 30 Days: Step-by-Step Implementation Plan
chapters.subtitle: Build one reviewed pilot workflow with explicit stop and continuation criteria.
chapters.executive_summary: The first month should produce one traceable operating experiment, not a promise of quick collections. Choose a single jurisdiction and recovery lane, establish the lawful scope of work, and protect the evidence before sourcing leads. Screen twenty official records through four explicit tests, then develop the strongest survivors into documented kinship packets with independent review. Finish with verified outreach or a recorded dry-run, an honest cost ledger, and a written continuation decision. Progress means learning which cases can be pursued accurately and economically, including learning when to close a weak lead.

key_metrics.label: Pilot scope
key_metrics.note: Do not mix probate and custodial recovery rules.

key_metrics.label: Screening sample
key_metrics.note: Official source entries, deduplicated before counting.

key_metrics.note: Collections are not required to measure process feasibility.

sections.heading: Days 1–7: select the lane and establish the workspace
paragraphs: On Day 1 choose one state and one legal lane: a defined probate research service or a specific custodial unclaimed-property recovery process. Write the selection on the pilot cover sheet, including the agency or court, target record series, proposed payer, and intended service. Do not mix tax-sale proceeds, probate distributions, and state-held property merely because all involve missing owners. On Day 2 retrieve the governing statutes, official forms, fee schedules, and agency instructions, recording their URLs and retrieval dates. On Day 3 give local counsel the actual proposed tasks and sample communications. Ask who may investigate, contact potential heirs, negotiate compensation, prepare filings, and represent a claimant; a generic business description will not resolve those questions.

On Day 4 document counsel's conclusions on private-investigator licensing, unauthorized practice of law, fee limits, contract timing, and any applicable exemptions. California Business and Professions Code section 6125 restricts practicing law in California to active State Bar licensees unless otherwise provided by law; factual genealogy does not authorize legal representation. Texas Property Code section 74.507 addresses agreements to assist recovery of property reported under that chapter, including timing and compensation restrictions that must be read against the specific facts. Neither citation supplies a national rule for every recovery lane. Record the current rule, its scope, and counsel's interpretation without importing a fee percentage from another state. If required authority is unresolved, continue source research only within the permitted scope and use a simulated outreach exercise.

On Days 5 and 6 configure the encrypted case vault, individual accounts, multifactor authentication, role-specific folders, and a backup recovery test. Create a case identifier format and separate source images, research notes, legal queries, correspondence, and financial records. Use a fictional case to test upload, redaction, restricted sharing, and restoration; do not upload live identity documents simply to discover whether access controls work. On Day 7 freeze the pilot budget and weekly hours, nominate an independent reviewer, and reserve counsel time for specific questions. Define what stops further spending: unavailable operating authority, exhausted cash budget, inaccessible evidence, or a critical unresolved identity conflict. The first week's deliverable is a usable work system with named owners, not a decorative business plan.

sections.heading: Days 8–14: screen twenty records with four explicit tests
paragraphs: On Days 8 and 9 pull twenty official probate or custodial records belonging to the selected lane. For probate, capture the docket number, decedent, filing court, relevant orders, personal representative if listed, and current procedural posture. For custodial property, capture the official property identifier, holder information, listed owner, amount if disclosed, and agency claim instructions. Deduplicate repeated entries before counting the sample, and record records that cannot be accessed rather than inventing missing amounts. Keep a source image or durable reference with retrieval date and distinguish the original entry from your transcription. A public listing is a lead, not proof that funds remain available or that a person with a similar name is entitled to them.

On Days 10 and 11 apply the four tests consistently. Gate 1 asks whether the asset and current custodian are verified through an official source. Gate 2 asks whether the jurisdiction, service scope, deadlines, and compensation route permit the proposed work. Gate 3 asks whether there is a plausible claimant identity or kinship chain that can be proved with accessible evidence. Gate 4 asks whether the likely collectible fee can justify remaining costs under conservative assumptions. Mark each pass, hold, or fail with a source reference and a reason. An unknown amount does not pass the economics test by default; it remains a hold until an approved bounded inquiry supplies enough information for a decision.

On Days 12 and 13 rank only the survivors, using estimated remaining effort and evidence quality rather than the largest advertised asset. A hypothetical ten-thousand-dollar potential fee with a twenty-percent collection probability has a two-thousand-dollar probability-weighted receipt before cost and timing adjustments; spending three thousand more cannot be justified by its headline value alone. These estimates are assumptions to test, not measured probabilities from a twenty-record sample. On Day 14 reconcile all twenty entries: survivors plus holds plus closed leads must total twenty. Use dead-lead reason codes such as duplicate, already paid, wrong identity, unavailable evidence, barred route, or uneconomic remainder. Retain a minimal audit record of closure so the same failed lead is not purchased again next month.

sections.heading: Days 15–21: build a proof packet that another person can challenge
paragraphs: On Day 15 select the strongest one or two survivors that fit available research capacity, not every lead that passed screening. Build a relationship question for each claimed link: whether the named child is the child of the relevant parent, whether two records describe the same individual, or whether a branch contains additional descendants. On Days 16 and 17 collect and correlate birth, marriage, death, probate, census, and other suitable records with full citations. Record access restrictions and use authorized channels for restricted vital records. A census household can suggest a relationship but may not establish the legal link needed for distribution. Preserve spelling variants, dates, residences, informants, and contradictions so the final conclusion is reproducible rather than dependent on the researcher's memory.

On Day 18 assemble a Genealogical Proof Standard, or GPS, packet: reasonably exhaustive research appropriate to the question, complete source citations, analysis and correlation, resolution of conflicting evidence, and a reasoned written conclusion. GPS is a genealogical method, not a substitute for the court's evidentiary rules or counsel's determination of heirship. Include negative search results with jurisdiction, date range, index searched, and search terms; absence from one index does not establish that a person never existed. Separate source quality from relationship confidence, and explain why a later informant's statement does or does not outweigh a contemporaneous record. Escalate unresolved conflicts instead of smoothing them out in a polished family tree.

On Days 19 and 20 prepare a provisional per-stirpes share table under counsel's identified governing rule. For a purely illustrative one-hundred-twenty-thousand-dollar distributable pool, assume three eligible child branches, one surviving child in each of two branches, and two eligible grandchildren representing the deceased child in the third. Under that assumed branch allocation, the surviving children receive forty thousand each and the grandchildren twenty thousand each. This illustration assumes away a spouse, debts, priority claims, and other complications; actual statutes may select another representation method. State every assumption, include all branches, and confirm the fractions sum to one. On Day 21 obtain independent QC sign-off covering identity links, citations, conflict resolution, and arithmetic, with counsel addressing legal distribution questions separately.

sop_steps.action: Apply the identified distribution rule to explicit assumptions.

sop_steps.action: Obtain a dated reviewer disposition.
sop_steps.detail: Close or explicitly retain every objection; do not call an author review independent.

callout.title: No outreach from an unresolved proof packet
callout.body: An attractive potential fee cannot cure a broken identity link.

Record reviewer identity, packet version, and corrections.
Use a dry-run if lawful outreach or proof remains unresolved.

sections.heading: Days 22–30: test contact, reconcile downside, and decide
paragraphs: On Days 22 and 23 prepare outreach only for reviewed cases within the documented permitted scope. Verify the contact route against appropriate records and minimize sensitive details in the initial message. Identify the firm accurately, avoid claiming government affiliation, and explain the service without promising an award or implying that a fee is required to contact the public custodian directly. Have counsel review the proposed agreement for the selected lane, including compensation basis, applicable limits, timing, scope, cancellation provisions where required, and who provides legal services. Do not send a recipient another family's identity documents. If a condition remains unresolved, conduct a dry-run using fictional contact details and record the exact reason live contact did not occur.

On Days 24 through 26 execute the permitted outreach or simulation and log the date, channel, approved message version, response, and next action. Respect a request to end contact and keep factual status updates separate from distribution advice. On Days 27 and 28 reconcile the time ledger, supplier invoices, record fees, counsel costs, and any remaining commitments. Model zero collections explicitly: if cash outlay is twelve hundred dollars and unpaid owner work is forty hours valued at fifty dollars, the pilot has twelve hundred cash exposure and thirty-two hundred economic cost before other omitted expenses. A signed contingent contract does not reduce that cash downside. Compare actual spend with the budget authorized on Day 7 and explain each variance.

On Day 29 prepare a decision memo that reports all twenty lead outcomes, reviewed packets, unresolved legal or evidence issues, actual hours, cash spend, and the next experiment's capped cost. On Day 30 choose Continue only when at least one reviewed pilot workflow is usable, the operating route is established, and the next bounded cycle fits available cash and capacity. Choose Revise when a specific repairable issue has an owner, deadline, and affordable test; identify whether the next cycle pauses outreach or changes sourcing. Choose Stop when the route is unavailable, proof cannot be obtained economically, or the loss budget is exhausted. No collections in thirty days alone do not establish failure, but absence of collections must remain visible in the cash plan rather than being replaced by optimistic pipeline value.

Test vault access and restoration before adding sensitive records.
